A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mmCooper work. Their complete main texts and supplementary materials, including equations, algorithms, tables and rendered figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments on OPV2V, DAIR-V2X and V2XSet, with component ablations, noise-robustness experiments and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and robustness results and adds communication-volume comparisons, inference-time measurements and fusion visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 3.5 and Figure 5 revise the specified DBA residual connection: v1 adds fused intermediate features after DBA, whereas v2 adds bounding-box features within DBA. The core filtering, two-stage fusion and losses remain. v2 Algorithm 1 retains the older residual, so this architectural revision is not consistently documented.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LiDAR-based cooperative 3D detection on OPV2V, DAIR-V2X and V2XSet, retaining the localization-error, heading-error and transmission-delay scenarios. The added bandwidth and timing analyses reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: Select2col is newly evaluated in Table 1 and Figure 6 and participates in the new timing comparison in supplementary Table 4. Previous Table 1 comparators and the Table 2 robustness comparator set remain. DisoNet/DiscoNet spelling changes refer to the same method.

E3.justification: Figure 6 adds communication-volume sweeps for Where2comm and ERMVP, and supplementary Table 4 introduces overall and component inference-time evaluation. Section 4.3 changes the reported GSP-removal control to disabling the entire CFG module's suppression and selection; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Existing splits, training budgets, backbone, AP metrics and noise ranges remain.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of efficiency and mechanisms: Figure 6 compares baseline bandwidth sweeps against mmCooper's operating point; supplementary Table 4 decomposes computation costs; Figures 7 and 12 visualize transmission selection and bounding-box calibration. The original localization, delay and heading robustness analyses remain, with their figures renumbered.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Gaussian standard deviations describe injected input noise, not uncertainty in estimated performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds bandwidth-tradeoff results, Select2col scores and inference timings, including 45.41 ms for mmCooper. Table 1 revises ERMVP's OPV2V AP@0.7/0.5 from 64.60/85.81 to 69.71/86.63 and V2XSet from 58.47/81.14 to 58.44/81.54. Table 3 changes DAIR-V2X intermediate-only results from 44.11/59.92 to 46.65/62.84 and late-only results from 46.21/57.02 to 45.78/56.88, reversing their AP@0.7 ranking. Headline mmCooper scores and Table 2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The DBA mathematical definition in Section 3.5 gains a bounding-box-feature residual, and Section 3.3 changes the Gumbel-filter numerator from g_f to the stage-specific g_f/b. These are limited mathematical specification revisions; no theorem or proof is added. Algorithm 1 is not fully synchronized with them.

C1.justification: The claimed novelty of adaptive intermediate/late-stage collaboration, robustness contributions and headline AP@0.7 margins of 7.29/1.31/2.09 remain. The revised abstract foregrounds confidence filtering already described in v1, without changing the core contribution's scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes some communication savings over late fusion to comparators transmitting boxes before NMS. Supplementary Section 3.5 explains computational efficiency through sparse transmitted features and sparse deformable-attention reference points. Existing robustness interpretations largely remain, without substantive new applicability limitations.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies CNN-based confidence generation, states that no additional model or data compression is applied, and specifies final NMS. It omits v1's explicit Gumbel-noise sampling formula and matched-identifier description of offset-loss targets. Hardware, training settings, voxel dimensions and shared-feature shapes remain documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds methodological and background references, including Gumbel-Softmax, straight-through estimation, detection losses, MACP and Select2col. It removes CARLA/OpenCDA citations and the discussion of Zhao et al.'s malicious-agent detection. Section 3.1 more strongly contrasts selective transmission with conventional full-scene transmission, while retaining the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 are extensively rewritten, with a revised conceptual overview, streamlined component terminology and expanded attention explanations. Communication-volume discussion becomes a separate experimental passage, and the supplement gains dedicated computation-cost and fusion-visualization subsections. This exceeds local copyediting.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 are substantially redrawn with revised flow, labels and explanatory captions. Table 1 becomes narrower and drops venue and communication columns, while Figure 6 presents communication-performance comparisons. New fusion visualizations and timing tables are added, and detection panels are recolored and reorganized. Existing robustness plots are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added bandwidth comparisons, computation breakdown and selection/calibration visualizations make the existing efficiency and mechanism claims easier to assess. Reworked diagrams also improve accessibility. These benefits are tempered by disagreement between Section 3.5 and Algorithm 1 about DBA residuals and the loss of exact communication entries from Table 1. The evidence supports a useful but limited overall improvement.
